title: Rohit Sharma's Childhood Coach Says India Need Him for the 2027 World Cup. The Critics, He Says, Can Keep Talking.
excerpt: Dinesh Lad dismisses fitness concerns over the 39-year-old opener, says his technique is built for 50-over cricket, and insists the next six months are crucial for the entire squad — not just Rohit.
body:
Rohit Sharma is expected to miss India's three-match ODI series against Afghanistan this month. A hamstring injury picked up during the IPL has not healed in time. The 39-year-old already lost the ODI captaincy last year, even after leading India to the Champions Trophy. His last ODI series, against New Zealand, produced just 61 runs across three innings. The question marks are everywhere: his age, his fitness, his future.

His childhood coach, Dinesh Lad, does not share any of them.

## 'He Doesn't Need to Prove Anything to Anyone'

Lad, who has coached Rohit since his formative years in Mumbai, came out swinging in an interview with PTI Videos on Friday. His message was unambiguous.

"Being a coach, I don't think he needs to prove anything to anyone," Lad said. "He badly wants to win the ODI World Cup. I have spoken to him and he is very categoric with what he wants in his career. I don't think he needs to prove his fitness. Despite the age factor, he is still fit enough."

The ODI World Cup is the one trophy Rohit has never fully claimed. India reached the final in 2023 at home, where they lost to Australia. He led the side to the T20 World Cup in 2024. But the 50-over crown remains the missing piece, and the 2027 edition in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia is, at this point, his last shot.

## The Technique Argument

Lad's defence went beyond loyalty. He pointed to the structural advantage Rohit has in the 50-over format — the ability to settle before accelerating, a quality that T20 cricket does not always reward but ODIs demand.

"Critics keep talking. It's their job," Lad said. "India needs Rohit's experience if we want to reach the finals. Technique-wise there is no problem. Moreover, in 50-over cricket, you need to settle a bit. Rohit has got such technique that allows you to settle and then launch yourself."

He also cited this year's IPL as evidence that Rohit's approach remains sound. "In the IPL also, he showed his technique. He wasn't only playing big shots but also taking singles and doubles. I don't understand the critics' point of view. My view is that he must be in the team."

## The Saba Karim Response

Former national selector Saba Karim recently said that the next six months are crucial for Rohit to confirm his place in the squad. Lad reframed the remark to apply to the entire team, not just one man.

"The next six months are crucial for all the players and not only Rohit," Lad said. "Everyone needs consistency to retain their place in the squad. Rohit will definitely play in the 50-over World Cup next year. He will perform well even after six months, but you will have to give him chances."

It is a reasonable point. India are in a transition period across formats. Virat Kohli, who was ruled out of the Afghanistan series due to injury, is also facing questions about workload and selection. Rishabh Pant just lost the Test vice-captaincy. The squad is being reshaped, and the debate over who stays and who goes is hardly limited to one player.

## The Numbers Behind the Debate

Rohit's ODI record is not the problem. In the 2023 World Cup, he scored 597 runs in 11 innings at an average of 54.27 and a strike rate of 125.95, finishing as the tournament's second-highest run-scorer behind Kohli. His career numbers in 50-over cricket remain among the best in history for an opener.

The concern is physical. After the IPL hamstring injury, Rohit is reportedly expected to report to the BCCI's Centre of Excellence on June 8 for a fitness clearance. Whether he is available for the Afghanistan ODIs will depend on that assessment.

Lad insists the injury is being managed, not ignored. "I have spoken to him," he said. The implication is clear: Rohit's focus is on the long game, not the next bilateral series.

## What This Means for NRI Fans

For the Indian diaspora, the Rohit question carries emotional weight that goes beyond stats. He is among the last of the golden generation still playing limited-overs cricket. His three double centuries in ODIs, his six IPL titles as captain, his role in the 2024 T20 World Cup win — these are woven into the way a generation of fans, many of them now settled in the US, UK, and Canada, understand Indian cricket.

The 2027 World Cup in southern Africa will be a major event for diaspora fans. Whether Rohit leads the batting order when India walk out in Cape Town or Harare will depend on the next year of performances. But his childhood coach, at least, has no doubts about the ending.

"Rohit will definitely play in the 50-over World Cup next year."
